_meta.description: High-resolution micro-step funnels for business scenarios

franchise_buyer.name: Buy a Franchise
franchise_buyer.description: Acquire and operate a franchise business — structured path with brand support but high capital requirements and ongoing royalty obligations
franchise_buyer.entry_point: Want to own a business but prefer proven model over building from scratch

stages.label: Desire to own a business — tired of working for someone else or want financial independence
Research franchise opportunities online — IFA, Franchise Direct, Entrepreneur Franchise 500
Attend franchise expo or discovery day — meet brands in person, compare 50+ concepts
stages.source: IFA Annual Report 2024 — 35K+ attendees at major expos

stages.label: Shortlist 3-5 franchise brands based on investment range, industry, territory
Request FDD (Franchise Disclosure Document) — 23 mandatory items, 150-400 pages each
Review FDD with franchise attorney — Item 19 (financial performance), Item 7 (costs), Item 5 (fees)
stages.source: ABA Forum on Franchising 2024 — only 50% hire franchise-specific lawyer

stages.label: Call 5-10 existing franchisees from Item 20 list — ask about real revenue, support quality, regrets
stages.source: Franchise Business Review 2024 — franchisee satisfaction survey

stages.label: Build financial model — estimate revenue from Item 19, subtract royalties (4-8%), marketing fee (1-4%), rent, labor
Submit franchise application — personal financials, net worth, liquid capital, background
Get approved by franchisor — they reject 50-80% of applicants for top brands
stages.source: Chick-fil-A: accepts <1%, McDonald's ~5%, avg brand ~30% — Franchise Times 2024

stages.label: Secure financing — SBA 7(a) loan most common, need 20-30% down, $100K-500K total investment
stages.source: SBA Lending Statistics 2024 — $15.2B in franchise loans

stages.label: Sign franchise agreement — typically 10-20 year term, non-compete clauses, territory restrictions
Find and secure location — franchisor typically has site selection criteria and approval process
Build out and renovate — must follow brand specs exactly, avg $150K-400K for restaurant concepts
Complete franchisor training — typically 2-6 weeks at HQ plus local training, mandatory
Hire and train initial staff — 5-30 people depending on concept, high turnover industry
stages.source: BLS Hospitality Turnover Report 2024 — 79% annual turnover in food service

stages.label: Grand opening — first 2 weeks typically strongest revenue due to curiosity, then steep drop
Survive month 1 — reality hits: actual costs vs projections, staffing issues, operational learning curve
Reach monthly breakeven — avg 18-24 months for food, 12-18 for service, 6-12 for home-based
Survive year 1 — 8% of franchises fail in first year vs 20% of independent businesses
stages.source: SBA Office of Advocacy Survival Rates 2024

stages.label: Reach meaningful annual profitability — avg franchise owner earns $80K-120K/year, wide range
Consider opening second unit — multi-unit operators own 54% of all franchise units
stages.source: FRANdata Multi-Unit Report 2024 — 54% of units owned by multi-unit operators

franchise_buyer.end_to_end_conversion: 12% — from initial research to profitable franchise owner within 3 years

digital_products.name: Sell Digital Products
digital_products.description: Create and sell digital products — templates, ebooks, Notion templates, Canva designs, courses. Low cost, high margin, but extreme competition and discovery problem
digital_products.entry_point: Have a skill or knowledge that others would pay $10-50 to access in packaged form

stages.label: Have a marketable skill or deep knowledge in a niche — design, productivity, coding, marketing, etc.
Identify what people actually need — search Reddit, Twitter, Quora for pain points in your niche
stages.source: Gumroad Creator Report 2024 — top creators spend avg 2 weeks on research

stages.label: Validate demand — check existing products on Gumroad/Etsy, see what sells, read reviews for gaps
Create first product — ebook, Notion template, Canva pack, spreadsheet. Avg creation time 20-40 hours
Set up on Gumroad/Etsy/Notion marketplace — create account, listing, connect Stripe/PayPal
Write compelling sales page — headline, pain points, benefits, social proof, pricing. Conversion depends on this
stages.source: ConvertKit Creator Report 2024 — sales page quality is #1 conversion factor

stages.label: Share on Twitter/Reddit/LinkedIn — first 48 hours critical. Most products get 80% of launch traffic here
Get first sale — median time to first sale: 14 days. 40% of products never make a single sale
Collect feedback from first 5-10 buyers — iterate on product based on real usage
stages.source: Estimated — best practice from top creators

stages.label: Create second product in same niche — builds catalog, cross-sell opportunity, signals commitment
stages.source: Gumroad 2024 — creators with 3+ products earn 4x more than single-product creators

stages.label: Build email list — lead magnet (free template), newsletter. Avg creator list: 500-2000 subscribers
stages.source: ConvertKit State of the Creator Economy 2024

stages.label: Reach $100/month — only 30% of Gumroad creators reach this level
Create a bundle of 3+ products at discount — increases average order value 40-60%
List on multiple marketplaces — Gumroad + Etsy + Creative Market + Notion. Each adds 20-40% revenue
Reach $500/month — top 10% of digital product creators
Build personal brand around niche — consistent content, recognizable style, authority positioning
Reach $1K/month — top 5% of creators. Usually requires 5+ products + audience + SEO/organic traffic
Create flagship premium product ($97-297) — comprehensive course, toolkit, or system
Reach $5K/month — top 1% of digital product creators, usually with email list 5K+ and strong brand

digital_products.end_to_end_conversion: 2-5% — from creating first product to sustainable $5K/month income
sources: ConvertKit State of the Creator Economy 2024

community_membership.name: Build Paid Community
community_membership.description: Build and monetize a paid community on Skool, Circle, or Discord — recurring revenue but high churn and constant content/engagement demands
community_membership.entry_point: Have expertise or existing audience that would pay monthly for access, accountability, and community

stages.label: Have genuine expertise or existing audience (1K+ social followers or email subscribers)
Choose platform — Skool ($99/month flat), Circle ($89-399/month), Discord (free but less polished)
Define clear value proposition — what members get that they can't get free on YouTube/Reddit
Set price — sweet spot $29-97/month for most niches, $197+ for high-ticket B2B
Invite first 10 members for free beta — friends, followers, existing customers. Need critical mass for engagement
Deliver value for 30 days — daily posts, weekly calls, resources. This is the audition period
Convert beta members to paid — expect 30-50% conversion from free beta to paid at launch
Get first 20 paying members — $1K-2K MRR. Critical mass for self-sustaining discussions
stages.source: Skool 2024 — 60% of communities plateau under 20 members

stages.label: Create evergreen content library — courses, templates, guides that new members access immediately
Host first live group call — Q&A, hot seat, workshop. Live events are #1 retention driver
stages.source: Skool Retention Data 2024 — communities with weekly calls have 2x retention

stages.label: Reach 50 paying members — $2.5K-5K MRR. Community starts to feel alive, organic discussions happen
Automate onboarding — welcome sequence, intro post template, buddy system for new members
Reach 100 paying members — $5K-10K MRR. Top 10% of Skool communities
stages.source: Skool 2024 — only 10% of communities exceed 100 paying members

stages.label: Deal with first major churn wave — months 3-4, members who joined on hype start dropping. Avg 18% monthly churn
Reach $5K MRR consistently — need ~75-100 members at $50-67/month with controlled churn
Add tiers or upsells — inner circle ($297-997/month), 1:1 coaching, annual plan with discount
Reach $10K MRR — top 3-5% of all paid communities. Usually requires strong personal brand + content flywheel
Hire community manager — $2K-4K/month, necessary to scale beyond 200 members without burnout

community_membership.end_to_end_conversion: 5-8% — from launching community to sustainable $10K MRR

gig_economy.name: Work in Gig Economy
gig_economy.description: Earn income through gig platforms — Uber, Grab, DoorDash, TaskRabbit, Fiverr. Fast money access but hidden costs, no benefits, and income ceiling
gig_economy.entry_point: Need money fast, have a car/bike/laptop, willing to trade time for immediate income

stages.label: Need money fast — unemployment, side income, flexibility, or transition between jobs
Download gig app — Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Grab, TaskRabbit, Instacart. Most sign up for 2-3 platforms
Complete registration — upload documents, vehicle info, banking details
Pass background check — takes 3-10 days, 5-8% rejection rate for criminal/driving record
First day working — learn the app, accept first rides/deliveries, anxiety and inefficiency
Learn the tricks — surge pricing patterns, best hours, high-demand zones, acceptance rate strategy
stages.source: Rideshare Guy 2024 — experienced drivers earn 30% more than new ones

stages.label: Complete first full week — 30-50 hours, gross $500-900 (before expenses)
Calculate real hourly rate — subtract gas, insurance, maintenance, depreciation. Gross $20-25/hr → net $12-16/hr
stages.source: MIT CEEPR Study 2024 — median rideshare driver nets $13.25/hr after expenses

stages.label: Realize hidden costs — gas ($50-100/week), car wear ($0.20-0.30/mile), insurance gap, no health benefits, self-employment tax 15.3%
stages.source: IRS Self-Employment Tax Guide + AAA Driving Costs 2024

stages.label: Decide to continue or quit — 50% of new drivers quit within first 3 months
Optimize routes and schedule — morning commute, lunch rush, Friday/Saturday nights, avoid dead zones
Work consistently for 1 month — establish routine, understand true earning potential
Deal with first bad rating or unfair incident — false damage claim, low tip, unsafe passenger
stages.source: Rideshare Guy Survey 2024 — 80% report unfair rating within 60 days

stages.label: Reach consistent $500/week net — requires 40-50 hours/week in most markets
Hit burnout/fatigue wall — physical toll, loneliness, monotony, back/neck pain from driving
Reduce hours or push through — many switch to part-time (20 hrs/week) or add second platform
stages.source: Edison Research Multi-Platform Gig Worker Report 2024

stages.label: Consider switching or stacking platforms — DoorDash + UberEats + Instacart for maximum flexibility
Reach $3K/month net — top 20% of gig workers, requires 45-55 hours/week in good market
Evaluate gig work vs traditional employment — factor in benefits, stability, career growth, taxes
stages.source: McKinsey Independent Workers Report 2024 — 60% of full-time gig workers would prefer traditional employment with same flexibility

gig_economy.end_to_end_conversion: 15% — from signing up to earning $3K/month net consistently after 6+ months
sources: Pew Research Center Gig Economy Report 2024

buy_existing_business.name: Acquire an Existing Business (SMB Acquisition)
buy_existing_business.description: Buy an existing small/medium business instead of building from scratch — faster to revenue but complex due diligence, financing, and transition risks
buy_existing_business.entry_point: Decide to buy an operating business rather than start one — seeking existing cash flow, customers, and systems

stages.label: Decide to buy instead of build — motivated by existing revenue, lower risk, faster path to ownership
Learn about business acquisition — read 'Buy Then Build' (Walker Deibel), take courses, join acquisition communities
Define acquisition criteria — industry, size ($200K-$1M SDE), location, owner involvement, growth potential
stages.source: BizBuySell 2024 — avg first-time buyer target: $250K-$750K asking price

stages.label: Search on BizBuySell, Flippa, BizQuest, LoopNet, brokers — 45,000+ listings active at any time
Review 20+ listings in detail — request P&L summaries, ask initial questions, filter for quality
stages.source: Quiet Light Brokerage Buyer Behavior Report 2024

stages.label: Submit 3-5 Letters of Intent (LOIs) — non-binding offer with price, terms, contingencies, timeline
stages.source: Harvard Business Review SMB Acquisition Guide 2024

stages.label: Get 1-2 LOIs accepted — typical acceptance rate 20-30% of submitted LOIs
Due diligence period (60-90 days) — financials, legal, operations, customers, employees, liabilities
stages.source: ABA Business Law Section — standard DD period

stages.label: Discover hidden problems — customer concentration, key-man risk, deferred maintenance, pending lawsuits, tax issues
stages.source: Quiet Light 2024 — 75% of deals uncover material issues in DD

stages.label: Renegotiate price or walk away — 40-50% of deals that enter DD fall through
stages.source: BizBuySell 2024 — 45% of deals in DD fail to close

stages.label: Secure financing — SBA 7(a) loan (up to 90% LTV, 10-25 year term), seller financing (60-80% of SMB deals include it)
stages.source: SBA Lending Statistics 2024 + Pepperdine Private Capital Report

stages.label: Close the deal — sign purchase agreement, transfer assets, fund escrow. Avg deal takes 6-12 months from first search
stages.source: BizBuySell 2024 — avg 8.7 months from search to close

stages.label: Transition period with previous owner — typically 30-90 days, learning operations, meeting customers, training
Take over full operations — owner leaves, you are now responsible for everything
First month running the business alone — fires to put out, systems you don't understand, employee anxiety
Retain key employees — 30% of key employees leave within 12 months of ownership change
Retain key customers — 10-25% customer attrition in year 1 is typical, especially with relationship-dependent businesses
stages.source: Quiet Light Post-Acquisition Customer Retention Data 2024

stages.label: Stabilize operations — maintain revenue, fix urgent issues, build trust with team. No growth yet, just survival
Improve operations — implement systems, reduce costs, improve marketing, add technology the previous owner didn't use
stages.source: Estimated based on acquisition operator reports

stages.label: Grow revenue 20%+ in year 1 — only 35% of acquisitions achieve this, but those that do see 3-5x ROI
stages.source: Searchfunder.com 2024 — 35% of SMB acquisitions grow revenue 20%+ in year 1

stages.label: Achieve full ROI on investment — typical 3-5 year payback period for SMB acquisitions

buy_existing_business.end_to_end_conversion: 5-8% — from deciding to buy a business to profitably growing it within 2 years. 80% of listed businesses never sell.
sources: Harvard Business Review SMB Acquisition Guide
